decisions.statement: The reading is taken on the workstation with the checkout.
The capacity is kept beside the readout the capacity was taken for.
The day is reached through the one module saying where a day is kept.
The day read is the day Alan opened rather than the day on the clock.
The stretches are reached through the module saying where a day is kept.
How to read a stretch's capacity is on the readout's own page.
The daily tracking declares no capacity key on a day row.
The capacity is `health-capacity-hours` on each stretch filed beside the day.
A day's capacity is a sum over that day's stretches.
Each stretch's capacity hours are worked out by the readout's own code.
Summing the stretches is the only arithmetic this module does.
A stretch is filed under the day's id rather than under the day's date.
The stretches are asked for in a read of their own.
The day is read before the stretches filed under the day's id.
A day nobody has opened is no reading rather than a capacity of zero.
A stretch with no capacity is left out of the sum.
A day where no stretch has a capacity is no reading.
The keys a stretch answers with are spelled back to the spelling the store keeps.
The guard summing the capacity is akasha's own rather than a guard rewritten here.
A run of this file takes a reading.
The root read is the root the environment states or the folder the call was made in.
An empty value in the environment states no root.
Where the readout's page sits is asked of the index rather than spelled.
The capacity itself is never printed.
Importing this file takes no reading.
Nothing here decides when a reading is due.

definition: the stress capacity Alan's stretches leave him, kept on the capacity readout
